subject: Renewal uplift: options to annualize midcycle top-up
messages:
From: Samira Patel <samira@brightscale.ai>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-01 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Mid-year top-up + co-term question

Hi Vivek,

Quick context: we hit the committed capacity faster than expected this quarter and procurement asked if we can place a mid-year top-up while looking at options to annualize the add-on so it aligns with our Jan renewal. Two questions:

1) Do you have a straightforward path to convert a mid-cycle top-up into an annualized commitment (i.e., move the additional capacity onto a 12-month addendum) and what pricing treatment would apply?
2) If we do a pure mid-cycle top-up (pro-rated), what uplift / discount can BrightScale expect?

We attached our Q2 usage export to help. Procurement would like a ballpark by end of week and a formal quote next week.

Thanks,
Samira Patel
Head of Cloud Ops, BrightScale
Attachment: usage_report_Q2.csv (csv)
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Samira Patel <samira@brightscale.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-01 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-year top-up + co-term question

Hi Samira — thanks for the data, that helps a lot. High-level answers below; I can put formal numbers in a quote after alignment with finance. Short version: yes, we support both a pro-rate top-up and an annualize path.

Options (ballpark):
- Pro-rated mid-cycle top-up: charged at list rate pro-rated for remaining term. Typical uplift: none; we can offer a small committed-use credit if you purpose the capacity to steady-state workloads.
- Annualize the add-on (move to a 12-month addendum with co-term to Jan): we can offer a blended effective discount on the incremental commit depending on size. For a ~+25% commit increase your account shows, we can look at a 5–10% effective discount vs. list (pending finance sign-off).

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal confirmation of the discount/credit approach (I’ll loop my manager for approval).
2) I’ll send two quote attachments: (A) pro-rate top-up, (B) annualized addendum with blended pricing + DocuSign link.

Do you have a preferred cadence for a quick call this week to walk procurement through the options?

Best,
Vivek Kulkarni
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
Attachment: RW_TopUp_Options_v1.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-01 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-year top-up + co-term question

Vivek — added a quick engineering note for context you can share with Samira and procurement: based on the attached usage pattern, we recommend sizing the top-up for steady-state baseline + 20% headroom rather than peak burst. That reduces required uplift and makes the annualize path much more attractive.

Suggested commercial framing we can use in the quote:
- Annualize option: 8% blended effective discount on incremental capacity if moved to a 12-month addendum and co-termed to Jan. We base this on 25% uplift vs current commit.
- Alternate: one-time operational credit (equal to ~6% of the mid-cycle top-up dollar value) in lieu of recurring list discount — preserves list price for benchmarking and satisfies procurement.

I left both options in the spreadsheet (tab: Commercial).

—Marissa
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-02 16:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Mid-year top-up + co-term question

Thanks for the clear framing. Quick internal decision: approve bringing two discrete options to BrightScale — (1) annualize with an effective 7% customer-visible discount on the incremental capacity, or (2) keep list pricing but provide a one-time credit equal to 6% of the top-up value.

Notes from finance/legal: prefer the credit path if procurement is sensitive to list pricing comparisons; prefer discount if the customer wants simpler bookkeeping and an updated subscription price. For deal hygiene, require that any annualize addendum be linked to the existing master agreement and include a month-to-month fallback for the first 30 days after co-term activation.

Vivek, please present both options exactly as written and include the finance-approved language. Let me know if you want me to join the call.

Laura Bennett
Director, Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
To: Samira Patel <samira@brightscale.ai>, BrightScale Procurement <procurement@brightscale.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-05 09:04:00 -0700
Subject: Renewal options — quote attached + next steps

Samira / procurement team — attaching two commercial paths as discussed. Short summary below and actionable asks at the bottom.

Option A — Pro-rate top-up (fast delivery):
- Add 150 inference units for the remainder of your current term (ends 2027-01-15).
- Billed pro-rata at list rate: $XX,XXX for remainder.
- No change to subscription price.

Option B — Annualize & co-term to Jan (preferred for unit economics):
- Convert the 150-unit add-on to a 12-month addendum, co-terming to 2027-01-15.
- Effective commercial: 7% discount on incremental annualized dollars (finance-approved).
- Includes a one-time operational credit if you prefer (6% of top-up value) as an alternate structure (capture in DocuSign).

Attachments: RW_Quote_BS-2026-147.pdf (pdf) — two quote variants inside.
DocuSign: https://www.docusign.com/embedded/abcd-1234-quote

Please confirm preferred option and whether procurement wants the credit or the discount called out on the DocuSign. If acceptable, I’ll issue the DocuSign envelope today and we can aim for execution next week. If you want to walk through the numbers, I’m available 11:00–12:00PT tomorrow.

Thanks,
Vivek
Account Exec, Redwood Inference
